result: Experimental evaluation on several datasets demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
conclusion: Geo-Privacy provides a practical approach to function privatization in the local model, balancing privacy and utility.

title: Weak But Not Strong Asymptotic Testability
authors: Senhan Yao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct two fixed disjoint families [MATH] of stationary ergodic binary process distributions for which a weakly asymptotically consistent test exists, but no strongly asymptotically consistent test exists. The construction combines a synchronizing binary suspension code, an independent i.i.d marker process, and countably many independent slowly switching two-state Markov chains. In particular, this disproves the asymptotic-consistency branch of a conjecture of Ryabko.
tldr: Constructs stationary ergodic binary processes where weak but not strong asymptotic testability holds, disproving a conjecture by Ryabko.
motivation: To resolve the asymptotic-consistency branch of Ryabko's conjecture by demonstrating a separation between weak and strong testability.
method: Combines a synchronizing binary suspension code, an independent i.i.d. marker process, and countably many independent slowly switching two-state Markov chains.
result: Two fixed disjoint families of stationary ergodic binary process distributions exist for which a weakly asymptotically consistent test exists but no strongly asymptotically consistent test exists.
conclusion: The asymptotic-consistency branch of Ryabko's conjecture is false; weak and strong asymptotic testability are not equivalent for stationary ergodic processes.

title: Self-similar Rigid Rotation In Anisotropic Squeezed Laguerre--Gaussian Beams
authors: D. Aguirre-Olivas, G. Mellado-Villase\~nor, B. M. Rodriguez-Lara
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce anisotropic squeezed Laguerre--Gaussian beams as an analytically complete family of structured paraxial scalar beams with Gouy-phase-controlled rigid rotation. Our construction organizes the Laguerre--Gaussian transverse modal Hilbert space into circular modal subspaces carrying parity-resolved single-mode [MATH] representations. The resulting optical Bargmann bases support squeezed states whose lowest-weight forms factor into Gaussian beam phases, parity-dependent polynomials, and elliptically anisotropic Gaussian envelopes. Excited seeds are polynomial deformations of the same squeezed envelope, extending the analytic construction to the full family. The Gouy-dressed squeezing parameter sets the semi-axis widths, aspect ratio, handedness, and orientation, while propagation rotates the profile by the accumulated Gouy phase without changing the scaled transverse shape. We generate these fields with synthetic phase holograms and experimentally confirm their self-similar rigid rotation. Our scalar-beam family provides a tunable anisotropic structured-light platform whose transverse orientation encodes propagation distance and may support axial localization, range finding, optical manipulation, and modal diagnostics.
tldr: This paper introduces anisotropic squeezed Laguerre-Gaussian beams that exhibit self-similar rigid rotation controlled by the Gouy phase.
motivation: To create a family of structured paraxial scalar beams with analytically tractable properties and potential applications in optical manipulation and metrology.
method: The authors construct optical Bargmann bases supporting squeezed states, derive the full family of beams, and experimentally generate them using synthetic phase holograms.
result: The beams rotate rigidly as they propagate, with the rotation angle given by the accumulated Gouy phase, and the transverse shape remains self-similar.
conclusion: This beam family provides a tunable platform for anisotropic structured light with potential uses in axial localization, range finding, and optical manipulation.

title: The Klein-Gordon-Fock Theory As A One-particle Relativistic Quantum Mechanics
authors: N. L. Chuprikov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Klein-Gordon-Fock (KGF) theory with scalar and vector potentials is presented as a one particle relativistic quantum mechanics (QM). First, the KGF equation is written in a Hamiltonian form, in spinor space; unlike the Feshbach-Villars approach, the Hamiltonian here is strictly Hermitian. Then this equation is rewritten for a one-component wave function. Expressions for the Hamiltonian and other observables' operators acting in the space of one-component wave functions are presented. The nonrelativistic and ultrarelativistic limits of these expressions are considered. A general solution to the KGF equation describing a free particle is presented.
tldr: The paper reformulates the Klein-Gordon-Fock equation as a one-particle relativistic quantum mechanics with a Hermitian Hamiltonian.
motivation: To resolve interpretational issues of the Klein-Gordon equation by presenting it as a consistent one-particle theory.
method: The KGF equation is written in Hamiltonian form in spinor space with a Hermitian Hamiltonian, then reduced to a one-component wave function.
result: Expressions for Hamiltonian and other observables are derived, and nonrelativistic and ultrarelativistic limits are considered.
conclusion: The KGF theory can be interpreted as a one-particle relativistic quantum mechanics.

title: Structure Of System-Specific Hazard Modeling For Physical Infrastructures In A Climate Change Context
authors: Matthieu Dutel
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses the definition and modeling of hazards in the context of physical systems, particularly infrastructures, that are affected by climate change. The paper highlights that hazards are system-dependent, meaning what constitutes a hazard for one system (e.g., humans) may not be the same for another (e.g., infrastructures). The paper also highlights that extreme intensity distribution may evolve in a region without necessarily constituting a hazard for a specific system. These distinctions are crucial for risk assessment and adaptation strategies in a changing climate. The paper implements a simple threshold-based hazard model -Boolean Hazard Model with Probability -to focus exclusively on system-specific hazard definition in climatechange context. Use cases illustrate how this approach adapts to different systems and hazard types. The model produces time-evolving hazard maps, delivering hazard data tailored to both hazard type and infrastructure characteristics. The model provides hazard data tailored to specific hazard types and physical systems, with a focus on infrastructure. The use cases demonstrate their practical value and potential for broader application in multi-infrastructure and multi-hazard exposure modeling.
tldr: This paper presents a threshold-based hazard model for physical infrastructures under climate change, focusing on system-specific hazard definitions.
motivation: Hazards are system-dependent and climate change alters extreme event distributions, requiring tailored risk assessment for infrastructures.
method: A Boolean Hazard Model with Probability is implemented to define system-specific hazards using thresholds, producing time-evolving hazard maps.
result: The model adapts to different systems and hazard types, delivering hazard data tailored to infrastructure characteristics.
conclusion: The approach shows practical value for multi-infrastructure and multi-hazard exposure modeling in climate adaptation.

title: Polynomially Improved Lower Bounds For Trifferent Codes Via Locally Sparse $3$-Uniform Hypergraphs
authors: Xuejiao Han, Yubo Sun, Gennian Ge
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A ternary code is if every three distinct codewords have a coordinate in which their symbols are pairwise distinct. Let [MATH] be the maximum size of a trifferent code of length [MATH]. The classical K\"orner--Marton construction gives [MATH] for an absolute constant [MATH]. We prove the polynomial strengthening [MATH] for an absolute constant [MATH]. Our proof refines the outer-code step in the K\"orner--Marton concatenation. We encode non separating triples as edges of a [MATH]-uniform hypergraph, randomly thin its vertex set, and remove high-degree vertices together with all remaining Berge cycles of lengths two and three. The resulting locally sparse hypergraph admits a large independent set by a theorem of Verstraete and Wilson, producing the additional factor [MATH]. Concatenation with the length-four Tetra code then yields the stated lower bound.
tldr: This paper improves lower bounds for trifferent codes using locally sparse 3-uniform hypergraphs.
motivation: Trifferent codes are a combinatorial object with applications in coding theory; improving their size bounds is a theoretical challenge.
method: The authors refine the outer-code step in the Körner–Marton concatenation by encoding non-separating triples as hypergraph edges, randomly thinning vertices, and removing high-degree vertices and short Berge cycles to obtain a locally sparse hypergraph, then applying a theorem of Verstraete and Wilson to find a large independent set.
result: They prove a polynomial improvement: the maximum size of a trifferent code of length n is at least n^{c log n} for an absolute constant c > 0.
conclusion: The work provides a new lower bound for trifferent codes via hypergraph methods, but it is purely combinatorial and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Disjointness-preserving Mappings On Calkin Operator Spaces And Positive Isometries
authors: Kai Fang, Jinghao Huang, Karimbergen Kudaybergenov, Ran Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let [MATH] and [MATH] be two Calkin operator spaces affiliated with a semifinite von Neumann algebra [MATH] equipped with a semifinite faithful normal trace [MATH]. We show that if [MATH] is atomless, [MATH] is finite, and [MATH], then every order-measure continuous and disjointness-preserving mapping [MATH] is identical to the zero mapping, which establishes a noncommutative version of Abramovich's theorem. We also show that every positive isometry [MATH] from a normed [MATH]-bimodule [MATH] of [MATH]-measurable operators into another [MATH] preserves disjointness provided that the norm of [MATH] is strictly monotone. As an application, we obtain the general form of [MATH], which extends and unifies several results due to Abramovich, de Jager, Conradie, Veksler and Sukochev et al. .
tldr: This paper studies disjointness-preserving mappings on Calkin operator spaces affiliated with von Neumann algebras, proving a noncommutative Abramovich theorem and characterizing positive isometries.
motivation: To extend classical results on disjointness-preserving operators to the noncommutative setting of operator algebras and Calkin spaces.
method: Uses order-measure continuous mappings and properties of semifinite von Neumann algebras, with strict monotonicity conditions for isometries.
result: Shows that under atomless and finite conditions, any order-measure continuous disjointness-preserving mapping is zero; positive isometries preserve disjointness under strict monotone norm.
conclusion: Provides a noncommutative generalization of Abramovich's theorem and unifies several prior results on disjointness-preserving operators.

title: Geometric Control Of Moving Parallel Transport In Riemannian Cucker--Smale Dynamics With Bonding Forces
authors: Woojoo Shim Hyunjin Ahn
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a Cucker--Smale type system with bonding forces on complete Riemannian manifolds with uniformly bounded curvature. On general manifolds, the time variation of parallel transport between moving agents produces curvature-dependent terms, so the standard energy-dissipation argument does not directly yield asymptotic velocity alignment. The bonding energy confines all pairwise distances below the injectivity radius, providing global well-posedness and time integrability of the transported velocity discrepancies. To overcome the remaining geometric obstruction, we combine the variation formula for parallel transport with a uniform endpoint estimate for Jacobi fields along moving minimizing geodesics. This yields the uniform regularity needed to convert energy dissipation into asymptotic alignment. Under an energy-dependent injectivity condition and a positive communication bound on the dynamically relevant distance range, we establish asymptotic flocking. Numerical simulations illustrate the resulting dynamics in a nonconstant-sectional-curvature setting.
tldr: This paper studies geometric control of moving parallel transport in Riemannian Cucker-Smale dynamics with bonding forces, focusing on asymptotic flocking on curved manifolds.
motivation: The authors aim to overcome curvature-induced obstructions to velocity alignment in multi-agent systems on Riemannian manifolds.
method: They combine variation formulas for parallel transport with uniform endpoint estimates for Jacobi fields along moving geodesics, under an energy-dependent injectivity condition.
result: They establish asymptotic flocking under a positive communication bound on the dynamically relevant distance range.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for flocking on manifolds with nonconstant curvature, validated by numerical simulations.

title: Compactly Supported Radial Basis Functions As Probability Density Functions
authors: Sergio D\'iaz-Elbal (university Of Almer\'ia), Andrei Mart\'inez-Finkelshtein (university Of Almer\'ia, Baylor University), Dar\'io Ramos-L\'opez
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26759v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compactly Supported Radial Basis Functions (CS-RBFs) are a fundamental tool in multivariate approximation theory. However, their use in statistics and probability modeling remains underexplored, having been used mainly to express covariance functions in Gaussian processes or as kernel functions. This work explores CS-RBFs as a novel parametric family of probability density functions, focusing in particular on Wendland [MATH] kernels. The primary contribution of this work is the derivation of analytical expressions for various statistical properties, such as moments and the cumulative distribution function, of CS-RBFs as univariate and conditional densities. The approach comprises two alternative scenarios: when the CS-RBF support lies entirely within the variable's domain (untruncated support) and when part of it is outside (truncated support). Mixture models employing CS-RBFs are also analyzed, and their main properties are detailed. Furthermore, we introduce an incremental learning algorithm for density estimation with CS-RBF mixture models, in which centers are determined using k-means and weights and shape parameters are optimized by stochastic gradient descent. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets show that CS-RBF densities provide competitive results in terms of likelihood and model complexity in comparison with Gaussian mixture models. In addition, these CS-RBF densities allow the exact computation of key distributional properties in univariate and conditional settings.
tldr: This paper explores compactly supported radial basis functions as a parametric family of probability density functions, deriving analytical expressions for statistical properties and proposing an incremental learning algorithm for density estimation.
motivation: CS-RBFs are widely used in approximation theory but underexplored in probability modeling; the authors aim to fill this gap by developing CS-RBF-based densities with exact computable properties.
method: Analytical derivations of moments and cumulative distribution functions for univariate and conditional CS-RBF densities, considering both untruncated and truncated support; mixture models with an incremental learning algorithm using k-means and stochastic gradient descent.
result: CS-RBF densities provide competitive likelihood and model complexity compared to Gaussian mixture models on synthetic and real-world datasets, and allow exact computation of key distributional properties.
conclusion: CS-RBFs are a viable alternative for density estimation, offering exact analytical tractability that Gaussian mixtures lack.

title: The Evolutionary Dynamics Of Ai, Politicization, Contestation, And Trust In Science Funding
authors: Animesh Ray
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Economic stability and progress in modern technological societies depend on vigorous and independent public funding of science and engineering research. When peer review or funding decisions are perceived as politically directed, scientists, funding agencies, and the public react in coupled and conflicting ways. We an evolutionary game-theoretic model to analyze how perceived political interference in science funding affects the interrelated behaviors of scientists, funding agencies, and the public. The model simulates scientists choosing to refuse peer reviews and retaliate, agencies responding by adopting AI-assisted review and altering reviewer pay, and the public accepting or rejecting these AI systems. Through numerical simulations, five principal findings are identified: (1) Operational capacity and institutional legitimacy are governed by separate conditions and can fail independently. (2) Legitimacy of the process is bistable, meaning final states are determined by the public's acceptance of AI. (3) Since the career cost for researchers refusing to review is generally low, resistance/retaliation cascades can readily ignite, leading identical institutions to entirely opposite fates. (4) Increasing reviewer pay only stabilizes participation within a strict budget-solvency frontier, and emergency pay can paradoxically erode the legitimacy it aims to protect. (5) Finally, finite-population simulations reveal that baseline scenarios partition into either legitimacy recovery without capacity or joint failure, confirming that the fundamental separation of capacity and legitimacy outcomes is a dominant structural feature driven primarily by initial scientific resistance and politicization levels. This theoretical work quantifies issues for future work in science policy.
tldr: This paper uses evolutionary game theory to model the effects of political interference and AI adoption on science funding dynamics.
motivation: To understand how perceived political interference in science funding affects the behaviors of scientists, funding agencies, and the public.
method: An evolutionary game-theoretic model with numerical simulations, analyzing interactions between scientists, agencies, and the public under different scenarios.
result: Five principal findings including bistability of legitimacy, low career cost for refusal leading to cascades, and separation of capacity and legitimacy outcomes.
conclusion: The model quantifies structural features of science funding systems, highlighting the importance of public acceptance of AI and the risks of politicization.

title: The Attention-Directing Ability Of Teams
authors: Olga Kokshagina, Marc Santolini, Christoph Riedl
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Why do some teams consistently mobilize collective effort and achieve superior performance while others struggle to coordinate action? We introduce Attention-Directing Ability (ADA), a latent team capability capturing how effectively members' interaction signals elicit engagement and coordinated responses from others. Extending the attention-based view, we conceptualize attention direction as an emergent coordination capability embedded in patterns of interaction rather than as a cognitive state or an outcome. Teams differ in the extent to which attention-directing signals trigger collective responses, and these differences shape how teams mobilize effort and perform. We examine ADA in a distributed innovation effort involving 2,233 participants collaborating asynchronously in 79 self-organized teams across 165 public Slack channels, generating over 30,000 messages. We model the causal responsiveness among interaction signals and derive a latent measure of ADA from teams' attention dynamics. We find that ADA strongly predicts both teams' likelihood of mobilizing engagement to sustain collective work and their performance conditional on participation. Correcting for self-selection into project submission, teams with higher ADA are more likely to submit proposals and achieve higher expert-evaluated outcomes. Causal mediation analyses show that these effects operate primarily through collective effort, indicating that attention direction functions as an upstream coordination capability. By conceptualizing attention as an emergent, measurable team capability, this study advances theories of collective attention and team coordination.
tldr: This paper studies team coordination and attention dynamics in online collaboration, with no connection to quantum information theory or quantum physics.
motivation: The authors aim to understand why some teams perform better by introducing a latent capability called Attention-Directing Ability (ADA).
method: They analyze interaction signals from 2,233 participants in 79 teams on Slack, modeling causal responsiveness to derive a measure of ADA.
result: ADA strongly predicts team engagement and performance, with effects mediated by collective effort.
conclusion: Attention direction is an emergent coordination capability that shapes team outcomes.

title: Mobility And Contact Networks Shape Epidemic Outcomes: A Large-Scale Agent-Based Modeling Study
authors: Kuldip Singh Atwal, Emma von Hoene, Hossein Amiri, Dieter Pfoser, Andreas Zufle, Taylor Anderson
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Human mobility plays a central role in shaping contact patterns that drive infectious disease transmission, yet mobility is often simplified in agent-based models (ABMs) due to data and computational constraints. The effects of these simplifications on model outputs are poorly understood. In this study, we systematically examined how alternative mobility assumptions influence emergent contact networks and epidemic dynamics within a large-scale ABM. Using a synthetic population of one million agents representing an urban environment, we implemented five mobility models varying along two dimensions: activity patterns (empirically derived vs. randomized) and destination choice mechanisms (empirical popularity, distance-based, or random). Holding disease parameters constant, we found that mobility assumptions alone produced substantially different contact network structures and epidemic trajectories, including differences in peak incidence and shifts in outbreak timing. Importantly, these differences could not be attributed to agents simply moving more or less overall since aggregate movement volumes were broadly comparable across models. Instead, the contrasting dynamics arose from how mobility generates contact opportunities: specifically, who meets whom, where, and how often. These results suggest that in models where mobility has not been carefully calibrated, simulated epidemic outcomes and evaluations of interventions may reflect mobility assumptions as much as underlying disease parameters. Our findings underscore the importance of mobility model calibration and validation, particularly in policy-facing applications.
tldr: This paper studies how different mobility models in agent-based simulations affect contact networks and epidemic outcomes, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Human mobility is often oversimplified in epidemic models, and the impact of these simplifications on model outputs is poorly understood.
method: Using a synthetic population of one million agents, five mobility models varying activity patterns and destination choices were implemented, and their effects on contact networks and epidemic dynamics were compared.
result: Different mobility assumptions produced substantially different contact network structures and epidemic trajectories, including differences in peak incidence and outbreak timing, even when aggregate movement volumes were similar.
conclusion: Mobility model calibration and validation are crucial for accurate epidemic simulations, especially in policy-facing applications.

title: The Boundary-driven Multispecies Harmonic Process
authors: Francesco Casini, Rouven Frassek, Cristian Giardin\`a
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the multispecies version of the harmonic process on a one-dimensional chain in contact with boundary reservoirs. This process is a continuous-time Markov chain where each site can host an unbounded number of colored particles. The symmetric bulk dynamics is put in contact with reservoirs, which inject and remove particles driving the system out-of-equilibrium. The Markov generator of the process is identified with the integrable Hamiltonian of an open rational Heisenberg spin chain of higher rank. We derive the underlying R- and K-matrices in operator form and construct the double-row transfer matrix following Sklyanin. Similar to the monospecies case the R-matrix factorises into two R-operators, each factor corresponding to left and right moving particles. We further define three dual models: an absorbing particle model, a hidden parameter model and a heat conduction model.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: On $R$-parastatistics I: Foundation
authors: Kaden R. A. Hazzard Zhiyuan Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parastatistics is an exotic type of exchange statistics beyond fermions and bosons. Paraparticles transform in higher dimensional representations of the exchange symmetry group, analogous to non-Abelian anyons, yet consistently defined in any dimension. Although paraparticles have long been proposed, they were widely believed to be physically equivalent to fermions or bosons. Nevertheless, a recent paper proposed a different theory, called [MATH]-parastatistics, and demonstrated that nontrivial [MATH]-paraparticles can emerge as quasiparticles in condensed matter systems, and are observably distinct from both fermions and bosons. This paper develops the theoretical foundation and several extensions of [MATH]-parastatistics, with particular emphasis on its observable consequences. Central to this paper is a general theory of local observables extending the basic family introduced before. First, we define local observables that distinguish particle types. Second, we formulate local observables at special point defects that probe the internal indices of [MATH]-paraparticles, crucial for observing [MATH]-parastatistics and for the proposed applications in quantum information. Third, we introduce local observables that create or annihilate particle-antiparticle pairs, important for building a relativistic quantum field theory for [MATH]-paraparticles. We further introduce generalized hidden symmetries that act on internal indices of [MATH]-paraparticles while preserving the local observable algebra, providing a basis for proving local indistinguishability and for connecting to a categorical description of [MATH]-paraparticles. This work sets a solid theoretical foundation for understanding the fundamental physical properties of [MATH]-paraparticles and pave the way for finding them in nature.
tldr: Analysis failed

title: Towards First Quantisation Formalism For Aksz Theories
authors: Pavel Mnev Leon Menger
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: \noindent Given an AKSZ theory [MATH] on a manifold [MATH], with target a graded vector space [MATH], we formulate a 1-dimensional theory [MATH] on graphs (the ``first quantisation picture for [MATH]''), whose partition functions reproduce the Feynman graphs of [MATH]. More precisely, the theory [MATH] is itself a 1d AKSZ theory with the target built out of [MATH], and involving a coupling to 1d supergravity. It yields a form on the space of metric graphs (with length [MATH] of an edge and its de Rham differential [MATH] interpreted as the zero-modes of the graviton and gravitino, respectively); its integral yields the sum of Feynman graphs of [MATH]. We study the theory [MATH] in the BV-BFV formalism; a gauge-fixing of [MATH] corresponds to a gauge-fixing of [MATH]. At the classical level, [MATH] assigns to vertices certain Lagrangian submanifolds [MATH] in Cartesian powers [MATH] of the phase space [MATH] of [MATH]. These submanifolds can be thought of as defining a cyclic [MATH]-algebra in Weinstein's symplectic category (``dequantising'' the cohomological vector field on the target %target AKSZ dg structure of [MATH]). In the path integral construction of [MATH], Lagrangians [MATH] determine sewing conditions for fields on the incident edges at a [MATH]-valent vertex. We give examples of this paradigm, such as when [MATH] on edges is the Witten-Morse supersymmetric quantum mechanics (which corresponds to a particular type of gauge-fixing for [MATH] and [MATH]). In the example where [MATH] is the non-abelian Chern--Simons theory with structure Lie algebra [MATH], we describe the vertex Lagrangian [MATH] (the ``Wigner Lagrangian'' ).
tldr: This paper develops a first-quantization formalism for AKSZ theories using a 1d AKSZ theory on graphs, linking to BV-BFV quantization and symplectic geometry.
motivation: To provide a graph-based first-quantized picture for AKSZ theories, enabling a systematic derivation of Feynman graphs and a geometric interpretation of vertices.
method: The authors construct a 1d AKSZ theory on metric graphs with target built from the original AKSZ data, coupling to 1d supergravity, and analyze it within the BV-BFV formalism.
result: The partition function of the 1d theory reproduces the sum of Feynman graphs of the original AKSZ theory, and vertex Lagrangians define cyclic A∞-algebras in Weinstein's symplectic category.
conclusion: This formalism provides a new perspective on AKSZ quantization and may unify various examples, such as Chern-Simons theory and supersymmetric quantum mechanics.

title: Generation Of High-fluence And High-intensity Hard X-ray Attosecond Pulses At European Xfel
authors: Ichiro Inoue, Ulrike Boesenberg, Rustam Rysov, Takahiro Sato, Ichika Harima, Chenzhi Xu, Jia Liu, Thomas M. Linker, Zain Abhari, Andrei Benediktovitch, Uwe Bergmann, Ye Chen, Lu Cao, Winfried Decking, Gianluca Geloni, Marc Guetg, Trey Guest, Aliaksei Halavanau, J\"{o}rg Hallmann, Takashi Kimura, Naresh Kujala, Aliaksandr Leonau, Shan Liu, Tianyun Long, Johannes M\"{o}ller, Taito Osaka, Jan-Etienne Pudell, Weilun Qin, Nina Rohringer, Angel Rodriguez-Fernandez, Daniele Ronchetti, Yasuhisa Sano, Matthias Scholz, Roman Shayduk, Jergus Strucka, Yanwen Sun, James Wrigley, Kazuto Yamauchi, Diling Zhu, Alexey Zozulya, Makina Yabashi, Anders Madsen, Jumpei Yamada, Jiawei Yan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By combining hard x-ray attosecond pulses from the European XFEL with total-reflection focusing x-ray optics, we generated nanofocused hard x-ray attosecond pulses with intensities and fluences comparable to the highest values attained in the hard x-ray regime. A peak intensity on the order of 10[MATH] W/cm[MATH] is confirmed through the observation of saturation in amplified spontaneous emission from copper atoms. These x-ray pulses enable new scientific opportunities, including the exploration of higher-order nonlinear light--matter interactions, damage-free structure determination, and coherent control of atoms and molecules.
tldr: This paper reports the generation of high-fluence, high-intensity hard X-ray attosecond pulses at the European XFEL using total-reflection focusing optics.
motivation: To enable new scientific opportunities such as exploring higher-order nonlinear light-matter interactions, damage-free structure determination, and coherent control of atoms and molecules.
method: Combined hard X-ray attosecond pulses from the European XFEL with total-reflection focusing X-ray optics to nanofocus the pulses.
result: Achieved peak intensities on the order of 10^20 W/cm^2, confirmed by observing saturation in amplified spontaneous emission from copper atoms.
conclusion: These nanofocused hard X-ray attosecond pulses enable new scientific opportunities in nonlinear optics and ultrafast dynamics.

title: Resolving Multiple Layer Thicknesses And Birefringence In Thin Films With An Optical In-line Roll-to-Roll Characterization Setup
authors: S{\o}ren A. R. Kynde, Astrid T. R{\o}mer, Abdelouadoud Mammeri, Jens W. Andreasen, Moises Espindola, Matteo Ciambezi, S{\o}ren A. Jensen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical techniques provide a fast and flexible path to material inspection. In particular, the investigation of key metrics during material production can help obtain the optimal parameters to achieve desired material functionality as well as to ensure product quality. Here we present an optical imaging setup designed for fast material inspection in a roll-to-roll deposition environment. The method allows for robust simultaneous determination of thickness in the range from 0.3 to 110 micrometers of multiple layers of transparent or semi-transparent materials in the form of a free film or a film deposited on a thicker transparent substrate. The PEDOT and ZnO materials chosen for this proof of concept are relevant for the fabrication of organic solar cells. Additionally, the method may be used to characterize birefringence.
tldr: This paper presents an optical imaging setup for roll-to-roll characterization of thin film thickness and birefringence, with application to organic solar cell materials.
motivation: Fast, non-destructive material inspection during production is needed to optimize parameters and ensure quality of thin films.
method: An optical in-line roll-to-roll setup is used to simultaneously determine thickness (0.3–110 μm) of multiple transparent/semi-transparent layers via imaging, and also characterize birefringence.
result: The method robustly measures thickness of PEDOT and ZnO layers, relevant for organic solar cells, and can detect birefringence.
conclusion: The optical characterization technique is suitable for inline quality control in roll-to-roll deposition of thin films.

title: On The Diophantine Equation $x_1^{3}-x_2^{2}x_1+1=0$ Over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2})$
authors: Pinki Khatun
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I investigate the Diophantine equation [MATH] where [MATH] and [MATH]. Using the arithmetic of the quadratic integer ring [MATH], together with norm arguments, divisibility properties, and the explicit description of its unit group, I prove that the equation has exactly two solutions, namely [MATH] As an application, I consider the family of elliptic curves [MATH] and deduce that, for every [MATH] the Mordell--Weil group [MATH] contains no rational point of order two.
tldr: This paper solves a Diophantine equation over a quadratic field and studies rational points on elliptic curves, with no connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The author aims to find integer solutions to a cubic Diophantine equation over Q(√2) and apply the result to elliptic curves.
method: Uses arithmetic of the quadratic integer ring Z[√2], norm arguments, divisibility, and unit group description.
result: Proves exactly two solutions exist and deduces that the Mordell-Weil group of a related elliptic curve family has no rational point of order two.
conclusion: The equation is completely solved, and a consequence for elliptic curves is established.

title: On Some Inequalities For Weighted Products And Ratios Of The Sine Function
authors: Augustine L. Mahu, Beno\^it F. Sehba, Cecilia D. Williams
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a reflection-substitution technique for sine inequalities that yields, via H\"older's inequality and its reverse, [MATH] distinct upper bounds for products and lower bounds for ratios of weighted sines. The comparison between bounds reduces to simple sign conditions on linear combinations of the variables. We fully classify the two- and three-dimensional cases, providing explicit dominance criteria with detailed examples for each signature.
tldr: The paper derives inequalities for weighted products and ratios of sine functions using a reflection-substitution technique and Hölder's inequality.
motivation: To establish new bounds for products and ratios of sine functions with weights, and to classify dominance criteria in low-dimensional cases.
method: Introduces a reflection-substitution technique combined with Hölder's inequality and its reverse to generate multiple bounds, then reduces comparison to sign conditions on linear combinations of variables.
result: Fully classifies two- and three-dimensional cases, providing explicit dominance criteria and examples for each signature.
conclusion: The technique yields a systematic way to obtain and compare bounds for weighted sine products and ratios.

title: Euler's $\ell$-totients And Riemann Hypothesis
authors: Ahmed Gaber
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26114v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a new analytic framework for investigating the Riemann hypothesis. For each fixed integer [MATH], define Euler's [MATH]-totient function [MATH] by \[ \varphi_\ell(n):=n\prod_{\\ v_p(n)\ge \ell}}\left(1-{p}\right), \] and its summatory function by \[ \Phi_\ell(x):=\sum_{n\le x}\varphi_\ell(n). \] An analytic study of the generalized Euler [MATH]-totient function [MATH] is carried out, including its Euler product representation, meromorphic continuation, and pole structure. For each [MATH], necessary and sufficient criteria for the Riemann hypothesis are established in terms of the asymptotic behavior of [MATH].
tldr: This paper develops an analytic framework for the Riemann hypothesis using generalized Euler totient functions.
motivation: The Riemann hypothesis is a central unsolved problem in mathematics; the authors aim to provide new criteria for its truth.
method: They define Euler ℓ-totient functions and study their analytic properties, including Euler product representation, meromorphic continuation, and pole structure.
result: Necessary and sufficient criteria for the Riemann hypothesis are established in terms of the asymptotic behavior of the summatory function of these totient functions.
conclusion: The work offers a new number-theoretic approach to the Riemann hypothesis but does not prove it.

title: On Phase-lock Area Parquet In A Special Slow-fast Limit Of Model Of Josephson Junction
authors: Alexey Glutsyuk
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26158v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: B.Josephson (Nobel Prize, 1973) predicted a tunnelling effect for a system of two superconductors separated by a narrow dielectric (such a system is called Josephson junction): existence of a supercurrent through it and equations governing it. The overdamped Josephson junction is modeled by the family of differential equations on the torus [MATH], [MATH], which is known as the RSJ model. It depends on three parameters: [MATH] called the abscissa, [MATH] called the ordinate, and a fixed frequency [MATH]. We study its rotation number [MATH] as a function of [MATH] and the phase-lock areas: those its level subsets that have non-empty interiors. They exist only for integer values of the rotation number (Buchstaber, Karpov, Tertychnyi). In this paper we study asymptotics of the phase-lock area portrait in a special slow-fast limit, as [MATH] and [MATH] so that [MATH]. We show that in the rescaled parameters [MATH] and [MATH] the phase-lock area portrait converges to a parquet with boundary lines being parallel to the lines [MATH]. Namely, the limit of phase-lock area with rotation number [MATH] is the union of an infinite chain of squares going up, with integer vertices and diagonals of length two lying on the line [MATH], and an infinite strip going down (sector in the case, when [MATH]). We state and prove a generalization of this result to a wide class of slow-fast systems on 2-torus.
tldr: This paper studies the asymptotics of phase-lock areas in a slow-fast limit of the RSJ model of a Josephson junction, showing convergence to a parquet pattern.
motivation: To understand the behavior of phase-lock areas in Josephson junctions under specific parameter limits, which is a mathematical problem in dynamical systems.
method: The paper analyzes the rotation number of a family of differential equations on the torus and studies the limit of phase-lock areas as parameters approach a slow-fast regime using rescaling and geometric arguments.
result: In the rescaled parameters, the phase-lock area portrait converges to a parquet composed of squares and strips, with boundaries parallel to certain lines.
conclusion: The result provides a complete asymptotic description of phase-lock areas in the slow-fast limit, with generalizations to a wider class of systems.

title: Inertial Primal Dual Dynamics With Hessian-driven Damping For Smooth And Bilinearly Coupled Saddle Point Problems
authors: Juan Peypouquet Zepeng Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Featuring Hessian-driven damping, two inertial primal dual dynamical systems are proposed for solving smooth saddle point problems with bilinear coupling. For convex-concave functions, we establish a convergence rate [MATH] for the primal dual gap; for strongly convex-strongly concave functions, we obtain an asymptotic rate [MATH] ([MATH] is the damping parameter) without knowledge of the strong convexity parameters, and an accelerated linear convergence rate when the strong convexity parameters are known. As an application of the proposed inertial systems, we also consider the affinely constrained convex optimization problem, and develop an inertial system with Hessian-driven damping, which complements existing results.
tldr: This paper proposes inertial primal-dual dynamical systems with Hessian-driven damping for solving smooth saddle point problems with bilinear coupling, focusing on convergence rates.
motivation: Saddle point problems arise in optimization and game theory; existing methods may converge slowly. Hessian-driven damping can accelerate convergence.
method: Two inertial primal-dual dynamical systems are introduced, incorporating Hessian-driven damping. Convergence rates are analyzed for convex-concave and strongly convex-strongly concave cases.
result: For convex-concave functions, a convergence rate for the primal-dual gap is established. For strongly convex-strongly concave functions, asymptotic and accelerated linear rates are obtained.
conclusion: The proposed dynamics provide improved convergence guarantees, with applications to affinely constrained convex optimization.

title: On Essential Freeness Of Actions Of Mixed Identity-free Groups
authors: Soham Chakraborty
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It was asked in [ACTT23] if every faithful, discrete, ergodic pmp action of a mixed identity-free (MIF) group is essentially free. In this short note we give some positive evidence by showing that for a MIF group, any faithful generalized Bernoulli action and any affine action on a compact abelian group is essentially free. This gives some classes of discrete ergodic actions with this property beyond the totally ergodic or compact case.
tldr: This paper studies essential freeness of actions of mixed identity-free groups in ergodic theory, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses a question in group theory and ergodic theory about whether faithful discrete ergodic actions of MIF groups are essentially free.
method: The author proves that for MIF groups, any faithful generalized Bernoulli action and any affine action on a compact abelian group is essentially free.
result: The paper provides positive evidence for the question by establishing essential freeness for two classes of actions beyond the totally ergodic or compact case.
conclusion: The results contribute to understanding the structure of MIF group actions but are unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Nonnegative Low-Rank Matrix Correction Under An Orthogonality Constraint In Conservative Vlasov Simulations
authors: Yue Wu, Stephen Becker, Jingmei Qiu, Xiangxiong Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In low-rank numerical methods for Vlasov dynamics, the SVD-type truncation procedure may introduce negative entries into the numerical solution. Such negative values are unphysical because the solution is a probability distribution function. We design optimization-based post-processing algorithms to recover nonnegativity while preserving the macroscopic quantities (density, momentum, and energy) pointwise. The preservation of the macroscopic quantities is written as an orthogonality constraint on the correction term. For a convex formulation based on squared nuclear norm minimization, we show that the proximal operator with the orthogonality constraint is characterized by an implicit singular value thresholding equation, and the threshold can be computed efficiently by bisection. Based on this result, we develop five algorithms for the convex formulation: Douglas--Rachford splitting, restarted dual FISTA, restarted dual accelerated gradient descent, dual PR+ conjugate gradient, and dual L-BFGS. We also consider a non-convex formulation with an explicit rank constraint and develop a tangent-space accelerated alternating projection algorithm that only requires a \(2r \times 2r\) SVD per iteration. Numerical results for a Landau damping test case show that the proposed algorithms give comparable correction quality. Among them, the tangent-space accelerated alternating projection is the most cost-efficient, increasingly so as the problem size grows. We further demonstrate the correction as a positivity limiter inside a time-dependent conservative low-rank Vlasov solver, where it removes the negativity introduced by the SVD-type truncation while preserving the conserved mass, momentum, and energy.
tldr: This paper develops optimization-based post-processing algorithms to correct negative entries in low-rank Vlasov simulations while preserving macroscopic quantities.
motivation: Low-rank numerical methods for Vlasov dynamics can produce unphysical negative values in the probability distribution function; the goal is to restore nonnegativity without violating conservation laws.
method: The authors formulate convex and non-convex optimization problems with orthogonality constraints to enforce conservation, and propose several algorithms including Douglas-Rachford splitting, dual FISTA, and a tangent-space accelerated alternating projection method.
result: Numerical tests on Landau damping show all algorithms yield comparable correction quality, with the tangent-space accelerated alternating projection being the most cost-efficient.
conclusion: The proposed positivity limiter can be integrated into time-dependent conservative low-rank Vlasov solvers to remove negativity while preserving mass, momentum, and energy.

title: Stabilization And Optimal $l^2$ Convergence Of Dziuk's Method With Piecewise Linear Parametric Finite Elements For Curve-shortening Flow
authors: Genming Bai
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26290v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a stabilized version of the fully discrete Dziuk's method for the curve-shortening flow of a closed planar curve with piecewise linear parametric finite elements. With a carefully designed stabilization term, we are able to show a surprising discrete tangential stability of the Barrett--Garcke--N\"urnberg (BGN) type under the parabolic scaling [MATH]---a feature hidden at the continuous level. Together with a new super-approximation result for the reversely averaged normal vector of linear elements, this Dziuk-type discrete tangential stability yields optimal [MATH] convergence.
tldr: This paper proposes a stabilized finite element method for curve-shortening flow, a geometric PDE, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To improve numerical stability and convergence of Dziuk's method for curve-shortening flow.
method: Introduces a stabilization term and proves discrete tangential stability and optimal L2 convergence using piecewise linear parametric finite elements.
result: Achieves optimal L2 convergence rates and discrete tangential stability analogous to the BGN method.
conclusion: The stabilized method provides a robust numerical scheme for curve-shortening flow.

title: A Cartesian Grid Method For Advection-Diffusion Equations With Robin Boundary Conditions On Moving Domains
authors: Han Zhou, Yoichiro Mori, Lingxing Yao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a Cartesian grid method for advection--diffusion equations with Robin boundary conditions on moving domains. The moving-domain problem is reformulated as an interface problem on a box, with an unknown density introduced on the moving interface to enforce the Robin condition. The bulk equation is discretized by a cell-centered finite-difference scheme on the Cartesian grid, while interface corrections are obtained from local problems in a narrow band around the interface. The resulting method requires only modest computational geometry, avoids remeshing and cut cells, and is compatible with geometric multigrid and matrix-free GMRES. The GMRES iteration count is essentially independent of the mesh size, and the computational cost scales linearly with the number of bulk degrees of freedom. For the one-dimensional scheme, first-order convergence in time and second-order convergence in space are proved. Numerical examples in one and two dimensions, including manufactured solutions and an active transport problem without an exact solution, demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the method.
tldr: This paper develops a numerical method for solving advection-diffusion equations on moving domains with Robin boundary conditions.
motivation: Moving domain problems with Robin boundary conditions are challenging for standard numerical methods due to the need for remeshing or cut cells.
method: The problem is reformulated as an interface problem on a fixed box, with an unknown density on the moving interface. A cell-centered finite-difference scheme on a Cartesian grid is used, with local interface corrections solved in a narrow band.
result: The method achieves first-order convergence in time and second-order in space for 1D, and numerical examples in 1D and 2D demonstrate accuracy and efficiency. GMRES iteration count is mesh-size independent, and computational cost scales linearly.
conclusion: The proposed Cartesian grid method is an efficient and accurate approach for advection-diffusion equations on moving domains, avoiding remeshing and cut cells.

title: Toward A Unified Statistical Theory Of Unsupervised Pretraining And Supervised Neural Knowledge Graph Learning
authors: Jifan Zhang, Miklos Racz, Suqi Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Knowledge graph learning provides a powerful framework for representing and inferring structured knowledge, with broad practical applications. However, the scarcity of relation-specific labeled triples per entity hinders the training of expressive models, and the ad hoc design of scoring functions limits generalizability and lacks theoretical grounding. We address both issues with a theoretically grounded, end-to-end training framework that extends and subsumes existing methods. Our framework is a two-stage procedure: unsupervised pretraining over heterogeneous corpora followed by supervised learning with multiple relation types. We establish a nonasymptotic risk bound that disentangles pretraining representation error from labeled-sample complexity, formally quantifying the benefit of large-scale unlabeled data for downstream knowledge prediction. Synthetic experiments validate each theoretical component, and real-world experiments confirm the effectiveness of our approach on large-scale knowledge graph benchmarks.
tldr: The paper proposes a unified statistical theory for unsupervised pretraining and supervised neural knowledge graph learning, with theoretical risk bounds and experimental validation.
motivation: Knowledge graph learning suffers from scarce labeled data and ad hoc scoring functions; the authors aim to provide a theoretically grounded framework that quantifies the benefit of unlabeled data.
method: A two-stage framework combining unsupervised pretraining on heterogeneous corpora with supervised learning for multiple relation types, analyzed via nonasymptotic risk bounds.
result: Established a risk bound that separates pretraining representation error from labeled-sample complexity; synthetic and real-world experiments confirm effectiveness.
conclusion: The framework subsumes existing methods and formally justifies the use of large-scale unlabeled data for knowledge graph learning.

title: Scalable Dynamic Optimal Transport Via Distributed Linearized Admm
authors: Hari Dahal, Rongjie Lai, Yangyang Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we address two fundamental challenges in the numerical solution of dynamic opti- mal transport (OT) problems. The first challenge arises when the initial and/or terminal densities approach zero and no positive lower bound is available. In this regime, conventional methods may become unstable or computationally inefficient, since the Lipschitz constant of the objective can scale like the reciprocal of the cube of the density. As a result, near-zero regions may lead to slow convergence or even divergence. The second challenge concerns the substantial memory cost of the dynamic formulation, whose discretization over fine spatial and temporal grids requires storing vari- ables across the entire space-time domain. This storage burden quickly becomes prohibitive as the grid is refined or the spatial dimension increases. To overcome the first difficulty, we reformulate the classical discretized dynamic OT problem so that the resulting objective admits an exact proximal mapping. When combined with a linearized alternating direction method of multipliers (LADMM), this reformulation yields an efficient and robust algorithm that remains stable even in challenging settings where the density may vanish. To reduce the memory burden, we further introduce a dis- tributed formulation in which the optimization variables are partitioned across multiple agents. This design substantially lowers the storage requirement for each agent and can also lead to computational acceleration. We validate the proposed framework through numerical experiments in one- and two- dimensional spatial settings under varying levels of difficulty. The results demonstrate the stability, robustness, and scalability of the proposed method in comparison with conventional approaches.
tldr: This paper proposes a distributed linearized ADMM algorithm for solving dynamic optimal transport problems, focusing on numerical stability and memory efficiency.
motivation: Dynamic optimal transport problems suffer from instability when densities approach zero and high memory costs due to space-time discretization.
method: The authors reformulate the discretized dynamic OT problem to enable exact proximal mapping and use a linearized ADMM; they also introduce a distributed formulation to partition variables across agents.
result: Numerical experiments in 1D and 2D demonstrate stability, robustness, and scalability compared to conventional methods.
conclusion: The proposed method effectively addresses both numerical instability and memory bottlenecks in dynamic OT.

title: On The Denseness Of Distal Points
authors: Su Gao, Hanfeng Li, Ruiwen Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an answer to a question of Xu and Ye (Disjointness with all minimal systems under group actions, to appear in Israel J. Math., arxiv:2212.07830) on the denseness of distal points in the Bernoulli shift [MATH] for a countable discrete group [MATH]. For a related but stronger notion of almost automorphic points, we answer the similar question by showing that the corresponding collection of the groups coincides with maximal almost periodic ones. These characterizations allow us to construct 2-step nilpotent groups for which the answers to the Xu-Ye question differ. In search for an intrinsic answer to the Xu-Ye question, we introduce a notion of point-distal radical for a countable discrete group and show that a necessary condition is for the point-distal radical to be trivial. Finally, we consider some related questions, and show that the collection of all countable groups [MATH] for which the set of distal points is dense in [MATH] is closed under finite-index extension, and that the collection of countable groups [MATH] for which the constant sequences are the only distal (almost automorphic) points coincides with the minimally almost periodic ones.
tldr: This paper studies the denseness of distal points in Bernoulli shifts for countable discrete groups, a topic in topological dynamics.
motivation: To answer a question by Xu and Ye about when distal points are dense in Bernoulli shifts, and to characterize groups with dense almost automorphic points.
method: Uses concepts from topological dynamics and group theory, such as distal points, almost automorphic points, point-distal radical, and constructions of nilpotent groups.
result: Provides a characterization of groups for which distal points are dense, showing it differs for 2-step nilpotent groups, and gives necessary conditions via the point-distal radical.
conclusion: The collection of groups with dense distal points is closed under finite-index extension, and those with only constant distal points are minimally almost periodic.

title: Model-Free Q-Learning For Infinite-Horizon Stochastic Linear Quadratic Problems With Regime Switching
authors: Xinyue Zhang, Na Li, Xun Li, Zuo Quan Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper addresses infinite-horizon continuous-time stochastic linear quadratic optimal control problems with regime switching. We propose a paradigm shift from model-based design by adopting an adaptive dynamic programming approach, specifically developing on-policy and off-policy Q-learning algorithms that learn the optimal controller solely from online state trajectory data. The theoretical core of our work consists of a complete proof of the equivalence between the on- and off-policy architectures, alongside a rigorous analysis establishing the stability of the closed-loop system and the convergence of the algorithms to the optimal solution. For computational tractability, we implement these algorithms using vectorization and Kronecker product algebra. The theoretical results are corroborated by numerical case studies that clearly demonstrate the operational effectiveness and practical feasibility of the proposed model-free control strategy.
tldr: This paper develops model-free Q-learning algorithms for infinite-horizon stochastic linear quadratic control with regime switching, focusing on control theory rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to solve optimal control problems without requiring a system model, using data-driven adaptive dynamic programming.
method: On-policy and off-policy Q-learning algorithms are proposed, with theoretical equivalence proof and stability analysis using vectorization and Kronecker product algebra.
result: The algorithms converge to the optimal controller and maintain closed-loop stability, validated by numerical case studies.
conclusion: Model-free Q-learning is effective for regime-switching linear quadratic problems, offering a practical data-driven control strategy.

title: A Receding Horizon Control For General Assembly Line Balancing Problems
authors: Luca Tirel Ali Mohamed Ali
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to the General Assembly Line Balancing Problem (GALBP) by utilizing a receding horizon optimal control framework. The proposed discrete model for the assembly line offers a flexible representation, avoiding assumptions about specific line configurations. The control actions aim to optimize the industrial assembly line by minimizing the completion time while adhering to constraints such as task precedence, workstation capacity, and resource requirements. Control actions are represented through task assignment and resource allocation matrices, assigning tasks to specific workstations and assigning resources to workstations, respectively. The optimization problem is formulated as a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) problem. The inherent robustness of the receding horizon approach ensures optimal solutions for the assembly line, effectively adapting to sudden changes. Numerical experiments demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed control synthesis in efficiently distributing tasks and resources, minimizing the overall completion time.
tldr: This paper applies receding horizon optimal control to the General Assembly Line Balancing Problem, an industrial engineering optimization task.
motivation: Assembly line balancing is a classic manufacturing problem; existing methods often rely on specific line configurations and lack adaptability to sudden changes.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Programming (MINLP) problem with task assignment and resource allocation matrices, solved using a receding horizon control framework.
result: Numerical experiments show the proposed approach robustly distributes tasks and resources, minimizing completion time while adapting to changes.
conclusion: The receding horizon control framework provides an effective and robust solution for general assembly line balancing.

title: A New Theorem Of Alternatives Leading To Sufficient Conditions For The Superiorization Guarantee Question Of Dynamic String-Averaging In The Inconsistent Case
authors: Yair Censor Kay Barshad
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Superiorization Methodology (SM) in the context of the General Dynamic String-Averaging (GDSA) method in the inconsistent case (that is, where the input operators don't have a common fixed point) which primarily aims at achieving convex feasibility while simultaneously reducing an objective function. In many scientific and real-world problems modeled as constrained minimization tasks, striving for the exact constrained optimum can be costly in terms of time, energy, and resources. Therefore, applying the SM can offer a practical and efficient alternative. In particular, we present a new "theorem of alternatives" for the superiorization method which leads to investigation of theoretical conditions under which the superiorized version of the GDSA algorithm converges to a "superior" feasible point, i.e., one with an objective function value that is smaller or equal to that produced by the unperturbed feasibility-seeking algorithm. While this question has only been partially addressed in the existing literature, we present new sufficient conditions that guarantee that the SM attains such a superior outcome.
tldr: This paper presents a theorem of alternatives and sufficient conditions for the superiorization guarantee of dynamic string-averaging methods in the inconsistent case, focusing on convex feasibility and objective function reduction.
motivation: The paper aims to address the theoretical gap in guaranteeing that the superiorized version of the GDSA algorithm converges to a superior feasible point, which is important for efficient constrained minimization in real-world problems.
method: The authors introduce a new theorem of alternatives and derive sufficient conditions for the superiorization guarantee of the GDSA method in the inconsistent case.
result: New sufficient conditions are presented that ensure the superiorized algorithm attains a superior outcome, i.e., an objective function value smaller or equal to that of the unperturbed feasibility-seeking algorithm.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical foundations for the superiorization methodology in the context of dynamic string-averaging, offering practical alternatives for constrained minimization tasks.

title: BiHom-L-R-smash Biproduct And BiHom-Yetter-Drinfel'd-Long Category
authors: Xiaoqian Liu Dongdong Yan
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we first introduce the notion of BiHom-L-R-[MATH]-smash biproduct over a BiHom-Hopf algebra, denoted by [MATH], where [MATH], and give the sufficient condition for [MATH] to be a BiHom-bialgebra. Furthermore, we describe the concept of BiHom-[MATH]-Yetter-Drinfel'd-Long bimodule via BiHom-L-R-[MATH]-smash biproduct bialgebra, and prove that the category [MATH] of BiHom-[MATH]-Yetter-Drinfel'd-Long bimodule is a strict braided monoidal category. Finally, for a finite-dimensional BiHom-Hopf algebra H, \((H){s,t,u,v}\) is isomorphic to the BiHom-[MATH]-Yetter-Drinfel'd category \({}_{H\otimes H^*}^{H\otimes H^*}{p,q}\) as braided monoidal categories.
tldr: This paper introduces BiHom-L-R-smash biproduct and BiHom-Yetter-Drinfel'd-Long category in the context of BiHom-Hopf algebras.
motivation: To extend the theory of smash biproducts and Yetter-Drinfel'd modules to the BiHom setting, which is a generalization of Hopf algebras.
method: The authors define BiHom-L-R-smash biproduct bialgebras and use them to construct BiHom-Yetter-Drinfel'd-Long bimodules, proving the category is braided monoidal.
result: They provide sufficient conditions for the BiHom-L-R-smash biproduct to be a BiHom-bialgebra and show an isomorphism between certain categories.
conclusion: The work contributes to the algebraic theory of BiHom-structures but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Primal Approach To Facial Reduction For Sdp Relaxations Of Combinatorial Optimization Problems
authors: Mingming Xu Hao Hu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26514v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a novel facial reduction algorithm tailored to semidefinite programming relaxations of combinatorial optimization problems with quadratic objective functions. Our method leverages the specific structure of these relaxations, particularly the availability of feasible solutions that can often be generated efficiently in practice. By incorporating such solutions into the facial reduction process, we substantially simplify the reduction steps. On average, our facial reduction algorithm is four times faster than the standard implementation on the considered benchmark sets, providing significantly improved preprocessing for SDP relaxations in combinatorial optimization.
tldr: This paper proposes a faster facial reduction algorithm for semidefinite programming relaxations of combinatorial optimization problems.
motivation: Facial reduction is a preprocessing technique for SDP relaxations, but standard implementations can be slow. The authors aim to speed it up by leveraging feasible solutions common in combinatorial optimization.
method: The algorithm incorporates feasible solutions into the facial reduction process to simplify reduction steps, exploiting the structure of quadratic objective combinatorial problems.
result: On benchmark sets, the algorithm is on average four times faster than the standard implementation, providing significantly improved preprocessing.
conclusion: The proposed facial reduction algorithm is more efficient for SDP relaxations in combinatorial optimization, offering practical speedups.

title: Bayesian Inference Of Discretization Error Means In ODEs Via Ensemble Kalman Filtering
authors: Yuto Miyatake Shoji Toyota
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a Bayesian framework to quantify discretization errors in numerical solutions of ODE models based on observational data. The discretization error is modeled as a random variable, and its mean-referred to as the discretization error mean-is inferred from the observations. By introducing a Markov prior on the temporal evolution of the discretization error mean, we formulate the problem as a state-space model with a linear Gaussian observation process, which enables efficient inference via the Ensemble Kalman Filter. We also propose a specific form of a Markov prior motivated by classical discretization error analysis, in which global errors accumulate from local errors. The proposed prior depends on the step size of a numerical solver, and we establish its convergence rate in probability as the step size tends to zero. Numerical experiments on the pendulum system and the FitzHugh-Nagumo model demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
tldr: This paper proposes a Bayesian framework to infer discretization error in ODE solvers using Ensemble Kalman Filtering.
motivation: Numerical solutions of ODEs suffer from discretization errors that are difficult to quantify; the authors aim to infer these errors from observational data.
method: The discretization error mean is modeled as a random variable with a Markov prior, and inference is performed via Ensemble Kalman Filter in a state-space model.
result: The method is validated on pendulum and FitzHugh-Nagumo models, showing effective error quantification and convergence in probability as step size decreases.
conclusion: The proposed Bayesian approach provides a principled way to quantify discretization error in ODE solutions using data.

title: Advanced Eeg Source Models From The Perspective Of Fem And Inverse Solutions
authors: Santtu S\"oderholm, Joonas Lahtinen, Sampsa Pursiainen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we compare forward solutions computed with finite element methods in Zeffiro Interface and DUNEuro, using the different source models they provided. We compared two of the source models from DUNEuro, called Whitney basis and Local subtraction, and the divergence-conforming model of Zeffiro Interface. For source estimation, we applied sparsity-promoting standardized hierarchical adaptive L1 regression (SHAL1R), standardized Kalman filtering (SKF), classical sLORETA, and dipole scanning. Analyses include Earth Mover's Distance, depth bias scatter plots, and qualitative assessments of amplitude distribution and focality. Preliminary experiments with source interpolation for each method revealed that Local subtraction closely matches expectations for the local behavior of the lead field at various depths. The main results reveal that the success of an inverse method depends strongly on the compatibility between its assumptions about the focality of the source and the chosen source model, with point-source models performing best when paired with methods designed for such sources, i.e., sparsity-promoting methods and methods that scan for a single source. Moreover, source models that admit patch sources with a wide distribution are more sensitive to additional noise.
tldr: This paper compares finite element source models and inverse methods for EEG source localization, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To evaluate how different source models and inverse methods affect EEG source estimation accuracy.
method: Forward solutions computed with Zeffiro Interface and DUNEuro using Whitney basis, Local subtraction, and divergence-conforming models; inverse methods include SHAL1R, SKF, sLORETA, and dipole scanning.
result: The success of inverse methods depends on compatibility between source focality assumptions and the source model; point-source models work best with sparsity-promoting methods.
conclusion: Source models that admit patch sources are more sensitive to noise, and method-model compatibility is crucial for accurate EEG source imaging.

title: Adaptive Gradient-Based Methods For A Broader Class Of Optimization Problems Under Performative Prediction
authors: Hiroki Hamaguchi, Yuya Hikima, Hiroshi Sawada, Akiko Takeda
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study optimization under performative prediction, where deploying a model affects the future data distribution. For this setting, several gradient-based approaches have been proposed. However, they typically assume specific data distributions or loss functions, which limit their practical applicability. To overcome these limitations, we propose a gradient-based optimization method with convergence guarantees under substantially weaker assumptions. Our method explicitly estimates the induced distribution shift through finite differences. It enables higher-dimensional optimization across broader classes of loss functions and data distributions. We also propose a practical variant that reduces the number of samples required. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our proposed algorithms converge faster and more consistently than existing ones.
tldr: This paper proposes gradient-based optimization methods for performative prediction, a machine learning setting where model deployment affects future data distributions.
motivation: Existing gradient-based methods for performative prediction assume specific data distributions or loss functions, limiting practical applicability.
method: The authors propose a method that estimates distribution shifts via finite differences and provide convergence guarantees under weaker assumptions, along with a sample-efficient variant.
result: Numerical experiments show the proposed algorithms converge faster and more consistently than existing methods.
conclusion: The proposed methods broaden the applicability of gradient-based optimization in performative prediction.

title: Optimal Control Problems For Quasi-linear Parabolic Equations And Their Linear Approximations
authors: Xu Liu, Meisai Wang, Xu Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by thermal diffusion models, a controlled quasi-linear parabolic equation can be formally replaced by its linear approximation, when the initial datum, target and control actions are sufficiently small. This paper makes this approximation precise at the level of optimal control problems. First, we provide verification criteria which distinguish whether an optimal control is an interior point or a boundary point of the admissible control set. We then prove that the differences between the optimal controls and the corresponding optimal trajectories for the quasi-linear and linear parabolic equations are higher-order infinitesimals with respect to the small initial datum and target appearing in the cost functional. Consequently, for small data, the optimal control problem governed by the quasi-linear equation can be approximated by the corresponding linear problem. In the interior-point case, the resulting approximation order is sharp.
tldr: This paper studies optimal control problems for quasi-linear parabolic equations and their linear approximations, motivated by thermal diffusion models.
motivation: To rigorously justify approximating a controlled quasi-linear parabolic equation by its linear approximation when initial data, target, and control actions are small.
method: The authors provide verification criteria to distinguish interior vs. boundary optimal controls and prove that differences between optimal controls/trajectories for quasi-linear and linear equations are higher-order infinitesimals.
result: For small data, the optimal control problem for the quasi-linear equation can be approximated by the linear problem, with sharp approximation order in the interior-point case.
conclusion: The linear approximation is valid for small-data optimal control problems, which is relevant for thermal diffusion models.

title: Mesh-dependent Iteration Count Growth In Primal-dual Active Set Strategies
authors: Michael Hinterm\"uller Ioannis P. A. Papadopoulos
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26622v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Primal-dual active set strategies (PDAS) are popular iterative solvers for mixed complementarity problems such as constrained optimization problems with pointwise inequality constraints. Examples include the reduced-space active set algorithm vinewtonrsls found in PETSc. When applied to discretized infinite-dimensional problems, PDAS exhibit local superlinear convergence thanks to their equivalence to a semismooth Newton method (SSN). However, for many problem classes the number of iterations, to reach convergence, grows without bound under mesh refinement. In this paper we numerically study PDAS iteration counts on uniformly refined meshes for obstacle problems, Signorini problems, and related models. As the mesh size tends to zero, PDAS applied to Signorini-type problems lose their local superlinear convergence, resulting in linear growth of the iteration count (adding some iterations with each refinement). For obstacle problems, PDAS stagnates, leading to exponential iteration growth (asymptotically doubling with each refinement). We explain these phenomena by (i) proving that, for obstacle problems, nodal degrees of freedom only peel away from the obstacle layer-by-layer during the deactivation phase, (ii) deriving a general global convergence rate for PDAS that depends on the magnitude of dual feasibility violation, and (iii) demonstrating why, in the infinite-dimensional setting, this leads to a well-defined solver, but without local superlinear convergence, for some problems yet divergence for others.
tldr: This paper studies iteration count growth of primal-dual active set strategies for solving constrained optimization problems under mesh refinement.
motivation: Primal-dual active set methods are widely used for solving discretized infinite-dimensional optimization problems, but their iteration counts can grow unboundedly under mesh refinement, which is poorly understood.
method: The authors numerically study PDAS on uniformly refined meshes for obstacle and Signorini problems, and provide theoretical analysis including a proof of layer-by-layer deactivation and a global convergence rate dependent on dual feasibility violation.
result: For Signorini-type problems, iteration count grows linearly with refinement; for obstacle problems, it grows exponentially. Local superlinear convergence is lost in the infinite-dimensional limit for some problems.
conclusion: The findings explain the observed mesh-dependent iteration growth and highlight limitations of PDAS for certain problem classes, suggesting the need for alternative solvers or preconditioning.

title: Hub Neighbor-Degree Diagnostics For Sparse Random Graphs
authors: Tiandong Wang Qian Hui
abstract: ArXiv:2607.26624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Networks with nearly identical degree distributions can place their hubs in sharply different neighborhoods. We develop a model diagnostic based on the mean degree of the neighbors of a degree-[MATH] vertex. Under rank-one inhomogeneous random graphs, this statistic has degree-invariant centering and [MATH] fluctuations. Under non-rank-one kernels, posterior uncertainty about the root type can instead determine both centering and scale. Under linear preferential attachment, the statistic grows as [MATH].
